name: Reference copy
belief: Assigning one variable to another copies the object, so changing one leaves the other unchanged.
pattern: b = a followed by b.append(x) or b[0] = x, with the student expecting a to stay the same.
correction: Both names refer to the same object, so a change made through one is visible through the other. Make a copy explicitly, for example list(a), a.copy() or copy.deepcopy(a).

name: Identity versus equality
belief: is compares the values of two objects.
pattern: Uses is to compare strings or numbers, for example if name is 'admin'.
correction: is checks whether two names refer to the same object. Use == to compare values, and keep is for checks such as is None.

name: Search bounds
belief: Any update of lo, hi and mid works as long as the interval seems to shrink.
pattern: hi = mid or lo = mid without adding or subtracting one, combined with a loop condition that can stall.
correction: State what is true about the search interval at the start of each iteration, and make sure every iteration strictly shrinks it. Test the two-element case.

name: Loop count equals complexity
belief: Complexity is the number of nested loops, whatever their bounds.
pattern: Claims O(n^2) for two nested loops where the inner loop runs a constant number of times or halves its range each time.
correction: Count how many times the innermost statement runs as a function of n, not how many loops appear in the code.

name: Constant-time lookup
belief: Dictionary and set lookup is always constant time.
pattern: States O(1) worst case for a dict lookup without mentioning collisions or the hash function.
correction: Constant time is the average case with a good hash function. The worst case can be linear when many keys collide.

name: Balanced by default
belief: Binary search tree operations are always logarithmic.
pattern: Claims O(log n) insert and search for a tree built from sorted input.
correction: Cost depends on the height of the tree. Without balancing, sorted insertions give a height of n and linear time.

name: Base case
belief: A recursive function works without a correct stopping condition, or the base case can be skipped.
pattern: No base case, or a base case that the recursive calls never reach, ending in a RecursionError.
correction: Every recursive path must move toward a base case that returns without recursing. Python stops deep recursion with a RecursionError, which is a symptom, not the fix. Trace the smallest input first.

name: Edit while iterating
belief: Removing items from a list inside a for loop is safe.
pattern: Calls nums.remove(x) or del nums[i] inside for x in nums.
correction: Removing items shifts the rest of the list, so the loop skips elements. Build a new list with a comprehension, loop over a copy such as nums[:], or loop backwards.
